units.translation: The epic poets constructed it, very rarely the tragedians, as the grammarian observed about Sophocles in Bekker's Anecdota p. 144, 22: about which I have spoken in my Lexicon Sophocleum p. 138. The examples in Aeschylus are also few and partly uncertain. Thus what is read at Pers. 791 μηδ᾽ εἰ στράτευμα πλεῖον ἢ τὸ Μηδικόν [not even if an army greater than the Median] is suspect because of πλεῖον [greater]. For the ancient Attic writers, although they said πλείων πλείονος πλείονα πλείω [more, of more, more (acc.), more (neut. pl.)] and the rest, nevertheless said πλέον [more] rather than πλεῖον [more], so that it is incredible that Aeschylus in this one place said πλεῖον ἢ [more than], when he could have written στράτευμ᾽ εἴη πλέον [the army might be more]. But Aeschylus does not seem to have written even this, but μηδ᾽ εἰ στράτευμα πληθύοι τὸ Μηδικόν [not even if the Median army should increase], to which was added the gloss πλέον εἴη [might be more], later changed into πλείον ἢ [more than]: just as the passive πληθύνεσθαι [to be increased], which has the same meaning as the intransitive πληθύειν [to increase], in Suppl. 604 δήμου κρατοῦσα χεὶρ ὅπη πληθύνεται [the ruling hand of the people, in whatever direction it is increased], is explained by the scholiast as πότερον πλείους οἱ συμμαχοῦντες ἡμῖν, ἢ ὀλίγοι [whether those fighting with us are more, or few]. Of no importance is Suppl. 400 μὴ καὶ ποτὲ εἴπῃ λεώς, εἴ πού τι μὴ τοῖον τύχῃ [lest the people ever say, if perhaps something not such should happen], where there is no doubt that Porson rightly wrote τύχοι [should happen]. A more certain example from the same play is 91 εἰ κρανθῇ πρᾶγμα τέλειον [if the matter should be accomplished perfectly]. and Eum. 234 δεινή τοῦ προστροπαίου μῆνις, εἰ προδῶ σφ᾽ ἑκών [terrible is the wrath of the suppliant, if I willingly betray them], where Porson wrote ἢν προδῶ [if I should betray].
